questions.q: What is P responsible for in PID?
options: It pushes back in proportion to the current error
It predicts the movement from the stick
questions.explain: P reacts to the current deviation: the larger the error, the stronger the correction right now.

questions.q: A drone hovers, but the wind keeps pushing it away and it does not return exactly to its place. Which PID term is responsible for this?
questions.explain: I accumulates a constant error and adds effort until it disappears.

options: It turns on air mode at zero throttle
questions.explain: D looks at the rate of change of the error and damps the overshoot.

questions.q: A D that is too high usually gives…
questions.explain: Hot motors and a “mushy” response: D amplifies high-frequency noise, and the motors work it off and heat up.

options: A contribution straight from stick movement
A doubled P on fast movements
questions.explain: FF reacts to the pilot's command before an error appears and speeds up the start of the movement.

questions.q: A P that is too high gives…
questions.explain: P overcorrects — the drone shakes at a high frequency.

questions.q: What is the D term computed from in Betaflight?
questions.explain: From the filtered gyro: there is no derivative kick when the stick moves.

options: It does not accumulate I on a sharp stick movement
It turns I off at zero throttle
questions.explain: It suspends I accumulation during fast stick movements; otherwise I adds extra rotation after a flip.
